note: Both define merchant-hosted agent checkout sessions; five status names match and both publish well-known discovery documents, but no bridge or mapping exists. Stripe co-maintains ACP and documents UCP for sellers who run their own checkout (its hub paired UCP or ACP until at least 2026-10-12). OpenAI's 2026-11-13 commerce plugin guide shows a reference checkout whose field names follow UCP's checkout schema rather than ACP's, without naming either, and Sierra's Personal Agent Protocol 1.0 carries commerce through UCP and does not mention ACP (2026-11-14).

Stripe co-maintains ACP and co-authors MPP with Tempo; MPP accepts cards through the same Shared Payment Token family, the token the ACP website names when it calls Stripe the first compatible PSP. Stripe's Link Agent Wallet also hands agents SPTs for MPP with method stripe (2026-11-14).

Visa Intelligent Commerce tokens under SPTs: Stripe says it might use them for SPT card payments, so Visa agent tokens can sit under an ACP payment. TAP itself has no documented link to ACP. Visa announced a strategic collaboration with OpenAI under Visa Intelligent Commerce on 2026-06-10 and is one of the three card networks among ChatGPT Wallet's named partners (2026-11-13); no source ties either to TAP, and OpenAI documents plain Web Bot Auth for ChatGPT's cloud browser, naming neither TAP's tags nor Visa's key store (as of 2026-11-21).

No documented protocol link. Stripe says it might use Mastercard Agent Pay tokens under SPT card payments. Mastercard is one of the three card networks among ChatGPT Wallet's named partners (2026-11-13), which OpenAI does not present as ACP; Mastercard's CEO said on 2026-10-29 that a broader OpenAI partnership includes the use of Agent Pay (reported), but no source names the program behind Wallet tokens.
ACP has no mandates or signed user intent; AP2 mandates or Verifiable Intent could add that layer, but no adopted extension exists.
